operations.name: init
operations.summary: Create or bring forward the instance in the data directory.
operations.exclusion_reason: Creates the instance in a local data directory. A running server already has one, so there is no meaningful remote semantics.

operations.name: migrate
operations.summary: Bring both stores forward to this build's schema.
operations.exclusion_reason: Brings the schema of the local data directory forward. Over HTTP it would be a request asking the server to change the ground it is standing on mid-flight; the server already migrates at startup , so the remote case is served by restarting it.

operations.name: status
operations.summary: Report instance identity, schema versions, and row counts.

operations.name: registry.dump
operations.summary: The operation registry as a manifest: every operation's scope, bindings, schemas and transport exclusion.

operations.name: instance.diagnostics
operations.summary: Deploy diagnostics: version, image digest, uptime, readiness checks, migration state and recent error log lines (redacted); peer=true also asks the configured peer instance (e.g. prod).

operations.name: engine.status
operations.summary: The session engine's operational report, as the GUI's Settings shows it: build, session / push / GUI-process counts, history archive and agent-task storage, workspace root, and event subscribers that fell behind. `engine` says why when it could not be asked.

operations.name: place.metrics
operations.summary: Read all bounded shell navigation counts in one response.

operations.name: connect
operations.summary: How to reach this instance, and the client configuration for doing so. Renders the connection document.

operations.name: mcp.stdio
operations.summary: Serve MCP over stdin/stdout until the stream closes.
operations.exclusion_reason: Takes over this process's stdin and stdout to speak MCP. That is meaningful only where the data directory is; a remote client uses the streamable-HTTP transport at /mcp. Offering it as a REST route would mean a server hijacking its own stdout.

operations.name: project.register
operations.summary: Register an existing folder or repository as a project.

operations.name: project.create
operations.summary: Scaffold a contract-compliant skeleton, then register it.

operations.name: project.import
operations.summary: Clone a GitHub repository into the import root, register it, and consolidate its existing forge state.

operations.name: project.get
operations.summary: Fetch one project by slug.

operations.name: project.list
operations.summary: List registered projects, each with `writable`: whether a default work.create lands there now, and why not.

operations.name: project.brief
operations.summary: The per-repo view: state, work, bugs, version, compliance. mode=summary (default) omits full items from top_backlog.

operations.name: project.update
operations.summary: Correct a project's declared repo URL or exclusions.

operations.name: project.transition
operations.summary: Move a project through its lifecycle states.

operations.name: work.create
operations.summary: Create a work item (feature / bug / chore / question).

operations.name: work.get
operations.summary: Fetch one work item with its relations, labels and comments (`id` is accepted for `ref`).

operations.name: work.list
operations.summary: List work items with filters, paged (limit/offset, next_offset). mode=summary (default) returns compact rows; mode=full returns whole items. `query` searches title/body/ref; `status`/`state` alias `states`.

operations.name: board.list
operations.summary: Read bounded, independently pageable Board cells in one snapshot.

operations.name: work.update
operations.summary: Change a work item's fields, assignee, or labels.

operations.name: work.transition
operations.summary: Move a work item to another state, validating the edge; a refusal lists the allowed edges and the shortest path. walk=true takes that path, one audited hop per edge.

operations.name: work.relate
operations.summary: Add a typed relation between two work items.

operations.name: work.unrelate
operations.summary: Remove a typed relation between two work items.

operations.name: work.bind_branch
operations.summary: Declare the git branch a work item is worked on.

operations.name: work.comment
operations.summary: Comment on a work item, attributed to the acting actor.

operations.name: backlog
operations.summary: The ranked backlog, globally or for one project, paged (limit/offset, next_offset). mode=summary (default) omits each row's full item; mode=full includes it.

operations.name: bugs
operations.summary: Open bugs across every project, ranked.

operations.name: why
operations.summary: Per-input score contributions for one ranked item.

operations.name: label.create
operations.summary: Define a label.

operations.name: label.list
operations.summary: List labels.

operations.name: initiative.create
operations.summary: Create a cross-project initiative with a ranking weight.

operations.name: initiative.list
operations.summary: List initiatives.

operations.name: initiative.update
operations.summary: Correct an initiative's title, body or weight, or close or reopen it.

operations.name: initiative.publish
operations.summary: Create or adopt one forge tracking issue per linked repo the initiative spans, each carrying a managed checkbox task list of its member work items. Additive and forward-only; a closed initiative proposes closing its tracking issues, never writes it.

operations.name: actor.create
operations.summary: Register a human or agent so work can be assigned to it.

operations.name: actor.list
operations.summary: List actors.

operations.name: workflow.list
operations.summary: The state machine each work-item kind is governed by.

operations.name: sweep
operations.summary: Run collectors over the registered projects.

operations.name: coverage
operations.summary: What has looked at what, and how long ago.

operations.name: observations.list
operations.summary: Raw evidence, including subjects ranked views filter out.

operations.name: deps
operations.summary: Dependency references out of a project, and into it.

operations.name: observations.prune
operations.summary: Apply the retention policy to observation history.

operations.name: suppress
operations.summary: Exclude an observed subject from ranked views.

operations.name: suppression.list
operations.summary: List suppressions.

operations.name: suppression.revoke
operations.summary: Revoke a suppression, returning the subject to ranked views.

operations.name: work.adopt
operations.summary: Promote an observed subject into a declared work item.

operations.name: contract.evaluate
operations.summary: Evaluate the contract against any path; stores nothing.

operations.name: contract.check
operations.summary: Evaluate the project contract; returns every failing rule.

operations.name: contract.adopt
operations.summary: Opt a project into the contract; it is not applied by default.

operations.name: contract.decline
operations.summary: Opt a project back out of the contract.

operations.name: contract.inapplicable
operations.summary: Declare that a criterion cannot apply to a project, and why.

operations.name: contract.applicable
operations.summary: Withdraw an inapplicability declaration.

operations.name: project.scaffold
operations.summary: Write the contract's skeleton into a registered project, never overwriting.

operations.name: compliance
operations.summary: A project's last recorded contract result, with its age.

operations.name: drift.detect
operations.summary: Compare declared state against observation; raise proposals.

operations.name: drift.list
operations.summary: Open drift proposals and their evidence.

operations.name: drift.resolve
operations.summary: Accept, reject, or contest a drift proposal.

operations.name: serve
operations.summary: Serve the API, MCP and health endpoints on one port.
operations.exclusion_reason: Takes over this process to listen on a port. A running server being asked over its own API to start another one is not a meaningful request; restarting a service is the supervisor's job.

operations.name: session.start
operations.summary: Open a coding session (a terminal) for a work item or a project. With `template` (e.g. claude) it runs that agent, and a `task` is delivered as the agent's first prompt, so it starts working instead of opening idle. Returns both ids (ses_… and engine_session_id); then poll session_screen until `ready`.

operations.name: session.list
operations.summary: List coding sessions with their live activity state (running / idle / waiting-for-input / exited / errored) and `alive`, including sessions opened from the GUI (unlinked, engine UUID only). Each row has both ids: `id` (ses_…) and `engine_session_id`.

operations.name: session.stop
operations.summary: Stop a coding session and revoke the token it ran with. Takes either id: Vogt's ses_… id or the engine's session UUID (an unlinked GUI session is killed, with no token to revoke). The process is killed; its screen and log stay readable.

operations.name: session.input
operations.summary: Type into a session: text, then named keys (enter, esc, tab, arrows, ctrl-c, ctrl-d, backspace), then Enter if submit. Takes either id: ses_… or the engine UUID. Read session_screen first and never send a blind Enter: at a menu it accepts whatever is highlighted (dismiss with esc). While a permission prompt shows, only a person's input is typed: an agent's is refused (403 person_required). Audited (byte count and keys, never the text).

operations.name: session.sweep
operations.summary: Oversee every session at once: one row per live or hibernated session with its activity, turn timing, last reply excerpt, blocked report, permission dialog and the last lines of its screen, ordered by who needs attention (approval, blocked, waiting, stalled, running, idle, hibernated) with the reason. Use this instead of session_screen per session.

operations.name: session.hibernate
operations.summary: Hibernate a session: stop its processes to free their memory, keep it listed (activity `hibernated`, with its last screen), and revoke its token. session_wake (or session_input, which wakes it) resumes the same agent conversation under the same id. Only for a session whose conversation id the engine knows (Claude Code started by Vogt, or any resume); a shell needs allow_shell and wakes fresh. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.wake
operations.summary: Wake a hibernated session: start it again under the same id, resuming its agent conversation in the directory it ran in, with a new token for the same actor. A live session is returned as it is. session_input wakes one by itself; wait for ready (session_wait) before typing after this. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.keep_awake
operations.summary: Pin a session awake so the engine's idle policy never hibernates it (keep_awake=true), or unpin it. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.rename
operations.summary: Rename a session, live or hibernated: the display name the GUI shows and session_list returns as `name`. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.remove
operations.summary: Remove a session: kill it if it still runs and have the engine forget it — its record, kept screen and brief — as the GUI's Remove does. session_stop keeps it listed with its output readable; this drops it. A linked session's record is closed and its token revoked as a stop would. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.set_role
operations.summary: Nominate a session as oversight (role=oversight): one that supervises other sessions. It is pinned awake, so it comes back by itself after a redeploy, and the GUI lists it first. role=worker makes it an ordinary session again and lifts the pin oversight set. Person-only. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.bind_work
operations.summary: Declare which work item a session serves (work_item=WI-n), or that it serves none (work_item=null) — one current item per session, re-declarable, audited. Any principal with work.write may bind: a person, the session itself (omit id inside a session Vogt started), or its overseer. Never moves the terminal or the item's state; the item then shows the session as being worked by it. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.grant_request
operations.summary: Ask a person to approve one scoped item for one live session (WI-973): a named credential (secret_name + project_id) the target then fetches with `vogt-agent-auth fetch VAR`. It appears in the Inbox; nothing is granted until a person approves. Ask for your own session, or — as an oversight session — for a session you drive. uses=once (default) or ttl; ttl_seconds 60..86400.

operations.name: session.grant_decide
operations.summary: Approve or deny a pending grant. A person's decision only: every agent is refused. Approval is applied to the live session by the engine before it is recorded.

operations.name: session.grant_revoke
operations.summary: Withdraw a pending grant or revoke an approved one at once. A person, or the session that asked, may.

operations.name: session.grant_list
operations.summary: Grants to sessions, newest first, by state (pending, approved, denied, revoked, expired) or target. Names only, never a value.

operations.name: session.answer
operations.summary: Answer the dialog a session shows (activity awaiting-approval) by choice: `option` (its number) or `label` (unique text of it); the engine moves the highlight itself. Startup gates (folder trust, external CLAUDE.md imports) take anyone's answer; a permission prompt (approval.kind permission or read-outside-cwd) only a person's — an agent is refused (403 person_required) and should leave it for the Inbox. Pass expect_question = approval.question so a stale answer is refused. Audited. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.token
operations.summary: The session engine's call: mint the agent credential of a session it started itself (GUI, protected template), bound to agent:engine:<uuid>, or revoke it (`revoke`). Refused to every other caller (403 engine_only). Gives such sessions an agent identity, so the core tells their agents from people. Audited.
operations.exclusion_reason: The session engine's own call, made over HTTP with its credential, to mint or revoke the agent credential of a session it started (WI-926). No person or agent has a reason to call it, and an MCP tool or CLI command for it would only put a refusal on every agent's tool list.

operations.name: session.screen
operations.summary: Read what a session's terminal shows right now: visible lines, cursor, title, activity and readiness. `ready` true means the program is waiting for input — wait for it before typing. Takes either id: ses_… or the engine UUID. Needs an engine with the screen route.

operations.name: session.last_reply
operations.summary: Read the last N replies of a session's agent (Claude Code or Codex) from its own transcript — whole, current and redacted, unlike the screen. Says how the conversation was found (`basis`). Takes either id.

operations.name: session.wait
operations.summary: Wait for a session instead of polling it: blocks (up to timeout_s, max 600) until it is ready for input — or needs a person (awaiting-approval, blocked) or exits — or, with until=exited / any_change, until it exits or changes at all. Returns why (`outcome`, `matched`) and the screen then. Takes either id.

operations.name: session.report_blocked
operations.summary: Report that this session's agent is blocked on a person: what it needs (`blocker`) and the concrete `items` to do. Shown on session_list/session_screen, raised in the Inbox and pushed; drivers stop re-prompting. Omit `id` from inside a session Vogt started. Clear with session_report_unblocked.

operations.name: session.report_unblocked
operations.summary: Clear a session's blocked report once the person has acted (or the agent found a way on). Omit `id` from inside a session Vogt started.

operations.name: agent_cli.list
operations.summary: Report the pod's agent CLIs: active, baked and upstream versions.

operations.name: agent_cli.update
operations.summary: Make a version of an agent CLI the one new sessions run.

operations.name: agent_activity.search
operations.summary: Search the tool calls agents made (from their transcripts, redacted): by text, service, tool, errors, time, project or session.

operations.name: agent_activity.summary
operations.summary: Per agent conversation: tool counts, error rate and time spent waiting on tools, for a session or a project.

operations.name: session.history_list
operations.summary: List archived sessions (history), newest first.

operations.name: session.search_output
operations.summary: Search session output (live sessions included).

operations.name: session.log_tail
operations.summary: Read the tail of a session's output log, readable — the history of what it printed, not its current screen (use session_screen for that). Takes either id: Vogt's ses_… id or the engine's session UUID.

operations.name: token.issue
operations.summary: Issue a scoped token bound to an actor. Shown once.

operations.name: token.list
operations.summary: List tokens. Never returns a secret.

operations.name: token.revoke
operations.summary: Revoke a token.

operations.name: auth.decisions
operations.summary: The allow and deny log. The denials are the interesting half.

operations.name: auth.whoami
operations.summary: Who the caller is, as authentication decided, and their scopes.

operations.name: auth.logout
operations.summary: Revoke the session or token this call arrived with.

operations.name: user.create
operations.summary: Give a human a username and password to sign in with.

operations.name: user.list
operations.summary: List logins. Never returns a hash.

operations.name: user.set_password
operations.summary: Replace a user's password, ending their sessions.

operations.name: user.remove
operations.summary: Take a login away. The actor and its history stay.

operations.name: backup
operations.summary: Snapshot both stores with a schema-version manifest.
operations.exclusion_reason: Writes to a path on the machine holding the data directory. Over HTTP the path would name a filesystem the caller cannot see.

operations.name: restore
operations.summary: Verify a backup's manifest, then replace the live stores.
operations.exclusion_reason: Replaces the live stores from a path on the server's filesystem, and every client's view of the instance changes underneath them. That is an operator action taken at the machine, not a request.

operations.name: clone
operations.summary: Restore another instance's backup here as a copy: keep this instance's id and credentials, revoke the source's tokens, disarm forge write-back, never copy push subscriptions.
operations.exclusion_reason: Replaces the live stores from a path on the server's filesystem, exactly as restore does, so it is an operator action at the machine for the same reason.

operations.name: export
operations.summary: Write the declared entities as JSON (format 2: with comments, relations and the clone stamp; --project for one).

operations.name: import
operations.summary: Merge an export into this instance under the documented conflict policy. A dry-run diff unless --apply --confirm; --strict refuses any both-sides change.
operations.exclusion_reason: Reads a file from the machine holding the data directory, for the same reason as backup.

operations.name: forge.onboard
operations.summary: Read a repository's existing issues, PRs, labels and releases into observations. Changes nothing upstream.

operations.name: forge.writeback
operations.summary: Set a project's write-back policy: none, comment_only, full.

operations.name: forge.link
operations.summary: Make a registered project upstream-truth: its work items become its forge issues, work writes go through, and any open native items migrate upstream.

operations.name: forge.publish
operations.summary: Create a repository under your forge credential, push the local default branch, and make the project upstream-truth. Refuses existing remotes; never force-pushes.

operations.name: forge.account_link
operations.summary: Link your own forge account by pasting a PAT, stored encrypted; upstream writes are then attributed to you.

operations.name: forge.account_status
operations.summary: Whether you have linked a forge account, and as whom. Never returns the token.

operations.name: forge.account_unlink
operations.summary: Remove your linked forge account; writes fall back to the instance file token.

operations.name: forge.repos
operations.summary: List the repositories your linked credential can see, so you can pick which to import (clone + full sync).

operations.name: forge.import
operations.summary: Import a repository the picker listed as a project: clone it under your forge credential, register it, and consolidate its forge state so it comes back linked and ready for write-back.

operations.name: forge.actions
operations.summary: The ledger of what Vogt has said upstream, and what landed.

operations.name: events.list
operations.summary: Read the cursor-based event feed.

operations.name: notifications
operations.summary: What GitHub is trying to say about the registered projects. Separate from the events feed, which is this instance's own history.

operations.name: deployed.versions
operations.summary: What each configured deployment lane runs (deployed SHA/version) against its branch head, with the commits and work items merged but not yet deployed. Read from the deploy-lanes collector's last sweep.

operations.name: inbox.list
operations.summary: List the normalized attention Inbox with coverage.

operations.name: inbox.archive
operations.summary: Archive one normalized Inbox occurrence.

operations.name: inbox.snooze
operations.summary: Snooze one normalized Inbox occurrence until a deadline.

operations.name: inbox.restore
operations.summary: Restore one archived or snoozed Inbox occurrence.

operations.name: preference.get
operations.summary: Read your own saved settings (e.g. inbox.filter), each with its version.

operations.name: preference.set
operations.summary: Save one of your own settings as a JSON object; {} clears it. Optionally only if it is still at expected_version.

operations.name: chat.list
operations.summary: List quick chats (persistent text chats with an agent, kept forever), newest first; `q` searches titles and everything said. `available` false means the engine has chats off.

operations.name: chat.get
operations.summary: Read a chat: its newest entries (agent text and tool results are untrusted data) and any approvals waiting for a person.

operations.name: chat.create
operations.summary: Start a quick chat with the engine's chat agent (Klaudia), optionally with its first message and a model the engine offers. Reads run at once; writes, commands and edits wait for a person's approval. Audited.

operations.name: chat.send
operations.summary: Send a chat a message and wait (wait_s) for the reply. A chat whose agent stopped for being idle resumes the same conversation. Audited (byte count, never the text).

operations.name: chat.decide
operations.summary: Allow or deny a chat's pending approval. Only a person may: an agent is refused (403 person_required) and should leave it for the person. Audited.

operations.name: chat.set_model
operations.summary: Switch the model a chat's next turn runs on (one the engine offers, or `default`). Audited.

operations.name: chat.interrupt
operations.summary: Stop the turn a chat is running. Audited.

operations.name: chat.archive
operations.summary: Archive a chat (hide it from the default list) or unarchive it. Nothing is deleted. Audited.

operations.name: chat.promote
operations.summary: Continue a chat's conversation in a terminal session (the agent resumes it there); the chat then takes no more messages. Audited.

operations.name: audit.list
operations.summary: Query the audit log.
